sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Area Operators
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the area of a parallelogram.
Zero determinant means area collapses to zero.
animations: Create a 2D plane with two vectors v1 and v2, colored #FF00FF and #00FFFF respectively.
Highlight the parallelogram spanned by v1 and v2 with a #FFFFFF fill at 20% opacity.
Display a target vector 'b' in #FFFF00 on the plane to show the goal.

sections.title: The Linear System as a Geometric Puzzle
lecture_lines: Systems of equations form a geometric puzzle.
Represent Ax equals b as a vector combination.
We solve for weights reaching the target vector.
animations: Draw a 2D coordinate system in #FFFFFF and plot vectors v1 and v2.
Animate v1 and v2 being scaled by coefficients to reach the vector b.
Flash the scalar weights used to scale the vectors to emphasize the solution.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule relates areas to variables.
Swap columns with the target vector.
Substituted areas scale with the unknown weight.
Ratio of these areas yields the variable.
This reveals the geometry behind the rule.
animations: Display the original parallelogram formed by vectors v1 and v2.
Visually swap one vector column with the target vector b.
Highlight the area of the new parallelogram in #FF5500.
Show the ratio calculation between the new area and the original area.
Display the resulting weight value next to the ratio calculation.

sections.title: Visual Proof: Area Scaling
lecture_lines: Area scaling proves the variable's value.
Watch the parallelogram expand and contract.
The area ratio equals the unknown weight.
This confirms Cramer's algebraic result visually.
animations: Display the original and the new parallelograms side-by-side in #FFFFFF.
Animate the scaling factor applied to the base vector.
Overlay the numeric area value calculation next to each parallelogram.
Sync the visual expansion of the area with the changing variable weight.
Fade out the scene to conclude with a proof of equivalence.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Constraint
lecture_lines: Singular systems have a zero determinant.
Columns collapse into a single line.
animations: Show two collinear vectors in #FF0000 on the plane.
Animate the shrinking of the parallelogram area until it collapses to zero.
Display the target vector 'b' clearly outside the line formed by the vectors.
